Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

The British National Party’s 2010 manifesto centres on national sovereignty, cultural identity, strict immigration control, withdrawal from the EU, law‑and‑order, economic protectionism, and expanded state control over key infrastructure.

- Defence and foreign policy: Withdraw troops from Afghanistan and Germany, avoid war with Iran, renegotiate NATO, raise defence spending, restore an independent nuclear deterrent, rebuild naval capacity, and introduce a compulsory year of community service for school leavers. Adopt a non‑interventionist foreign policy, end foreign aid, and engage the Islamic world on a non‑interference basis.

- Immigration and Islam: Halt all new immigration; deport illegal immigrants and foreign offenders; review post‑1997 citizenship grants; expand border enforcement; promote voluntary repatriation. The party portrays Islam as incompatible with Western democracy, proposes banning the burka, ritual slaughter, and new mosques, ending immigration from Muslim‑majority countries, and deporting radical preachers. It links terrorism to immigration and foreign policy.

- Civil liberties and constitution: Repeal the Human Rights Act, withdraw from the ECHR, roll back speech laws on race and religion, reject ID cards, and revoke the European Arrest Warrant. Create an English parliament, a pan‑British parliament (inviting Ireland), devolve powers to restored county councils, reform the Lords with non‑party experts, introduce citizens’ initiative referenda, a new Bill of Rights, tighter postal voting rules, and new media rules including a right of reply and penalties for deliberate falsehoods.

- EU and economy: Leave the EU to regain legislative control and stop contributions, pursue bilateral trade (especially with Commonwealth partners), and oppose Turkish accession. Fund deficit reduction by cutting spending on EU membership, foreign aid, climate programmes, wars, and “politically correct” bodies. Raise the income tax personal allowance to £12,500, restore a married allowance, lift the inheritance tax threshold to £1m, and cut council tax by scrapping “diversity” functions. Promote protectionism, scrutinise foreign takeovers, curb multinational tax avoidance, separate retail and investment banking, oppose privatising natural monopolies, and support SMEs. Expand credit unions and explore local currencies.

- Public services: Restrict welfare, social housing, and NHS access to Britons and contributors; shift from welfare to workfare; prioritise British hiring in the NHS; end “health tourism”; reverse NHS privatisation trends; cut bureaucracy; restore ward‑based cleaning.

- Law, culture, and education: Toughen policing and sentencing, including corporal and capital punishment in defined cases; expand prisoners’ hard labour; strengthen householders’ self‑defence rights. Promote British history and traditions; protect pubs; tax large supermarkets to aid high streets; add saints’ days as holidays. Restore traditional curricula, streaming and grammar schools, more apprenticeships, competitive sport, and free university for those completing community service; prioritise STEM.

- Infrastructure, environment, and energy: Reverse rail privatisation; invest in high‑speed rail; cut fuel taxes; toll foreign trucks. End most green‑belt building by curbing demand; apply “polluter pays”; favour brownfield development; reject wind expansion and climate legislation; expand nuclear (British‑owned), clean coal, and R&D in wave/hydrogen. In agriculture and fisheries: phase out CAP with UK support, ban GM crops and non‑stunned slaughter, back family farms, and restore a 200‑mile fishing limit.

- Housing and pensions: Empower councils to build for British citizens with local‑connection tests; create an infrastructure bank; attribute housing pressure to immigration. Raise the state pension toward £150/week, link to earnings, gradually raise retirement age, cap pension tax relief, and limit eligibility to Britons and full contributors.

- IT: Invest in technology universities, protect domestic IT jobs, nationalise telecoms infrastructure to deliver universal 100 Mbps broadband, and strengthen personal data rights.

TEXT_G:
UKIP Manifesto 2010 – Summary (under 500 words)

Core vision
- Leave the European Union to restore sovereignty, lawmaking and border control; reclaim funds (ending net contributions), scrap EU regulations, and reassert UK courts and Parliament. Introduce binding national/local referenda and more directly elected local boards.

Economy, tax and regulation
- Radical tax simplification: raise personal allowance to £11,500; introduce a 31% flat income tax merging NI; phase out Employers’ NI over five years; abolish Inheritance Tax when affordable.
- Replace VAT with a Local Sales Tax, with a share going directly to councils; return 50% of business rates locally; cut council tax by axing EU-driven costs (e.g., landfill rules).
- Major public spending cuts via quango culls and shrinking the state to 1997 size while protecting frontline services.
- Scrap up to 120,000 EU rules; restore Bank of England prudential control; separate retail/investment banking (Glass–Steagall style); raise capital ratios; reintroduce a lending “corset.”

Jobs, enterprise and skills
- Create c.1m skilled jobs via long-term programmes: defence re-equipment, nuclear build-out, flood/coastal defences, transport upgrades (rail/roads/ports/airports), and prison construction.
- Production Enterprise Centres for SME support; amend takeover rules to protect strategic firms.
- Denationalise universities/FE via Student/Training Vouchers usable in adulthood.

Immigration and asylum
- Five-year freeze on permanent immigration; long-term cap at about 50,000 p.a.; points-based system thereafter.
- Leave the EU to regain border control; triple UKBA staff; no amnesties; mandatory visas/health insurance; tougher asylum processing; reinstate Primary Purpose Rule; repeal Human Rights Act and leave ECHR; end state promotion of multiculturalism.

Law and order
- Directly elected Police Boards; zero tolerance; life means life; double prison capacity; three-strikes policy; boot camps; restore UK extradition safeguards; abolish CPS.

Defence
- Increase defence spending by 40%; expand Army and TA; three carriers and larger fleet; more RAF lift/rotary; maintain/replace Trident; prioritise NATO; reassess Afghanistan; cut MoD bureaucracy; improve forces’ pay and care.

NHS
- No frontline cuts; elected County Health Boards; abolish SHAs/PCTs; franchise services within fixed budgets; Health Credit Vouchers to opt out; restore matrons; bring back free eye tests and dental check-ups.

Education
- School Vouchers; protect/expand grammar and new “professional” schools; basic skills focus; tougher teacher standards; end 50% uni target; restore grants via vouchers; elected Education Boards; franchise schools; lighter, teacher-led inspection; support special schools and home education.

Pensions and welfare
- Flat, non-means-tested Citizen’s Pension of at least £130/week; restore dividend tax credit; freeze unfunded public sector pensions; leave EU pensions integration.
- Merge benefits into a single Basic Cash Benefit aligned with work; enhance Child/Nursery support via vouchers; restrict benefits to citizens/residents of 5+ years; introduce Workfare.

Foreign affairs and trade
- Leave EU; seek Swiss-style FTA; reclaim WTO seat; pursue Commonwealth Free Trade Area and other global deals; back democracy (e.g., Tibet, Burma, Taiwan).

Energy and environment
- Climate sceptic stance: repeal Climate Change Act; expand nuclear to 50% of electricity; support domestic coal; curb wind (offshore only, market-funded); exit EU carbon schemes; set up a Royal Commission; promote EVs and rail electrification; strengthen flood/coastal defences.

Transport
- +£3bn/year infrastructure; new bypasses and road widening; fuel duty “windfall return”; Britdisc for foreign lorries; three new high-speed rail lines; reopen lines; shift freight to rail/canals; oppose Heathrow expansion in favour of a Thames Estuary hub.

Housing and planning
- Reduce demand by curbing immigration; use empty homes; abolish regional strategies/IPC/RDAs; local binding referenda on major schemes; Green Belt conservators; scrap Section 106/social housing mandates; remove empty property rates; council bond-funded social housing.

Constitution and governance
- Direct democracy (5% trigger for referenda); AV+ electoral reform; elected police/health/education boards; replace devolved members with Westminster MPs; English-only days; MP recall; abolish regional government; support monarchy/Church; Parliament to ratify treaties and war.

Culture and Britishness
- Civic nationalism; oppose multiculturalism; protect British brands/weights/measures; strengthen Royal Mail/Post Offices; teach British contributions; restrict burqa/niqab in public buildings; deport radical preachers; reinstate Treason Act; Sharia can’t override UK law; Commonwealth Day; English Parliament; St George’s Day holiday.

Food, farming and countryside
- Leave EU; maintain support while shifting to pro-British labelling; ethical and GM labelling; ease EU nitrate rules; support producer co-ops and a supermarket ombudsman; local referenda to reverse hunting ban.

Fishing
- Leave CFP; reclaim a 200nm EEZ; end discards and quotas; mandatory landing; movable no-take zones; ban industrial/pair trawling; strengthen protection.

Other
- Strong animal welfare; protect pubs with designated smoking rooms; back SMEs; safeguard Royal Mail/Post Offices.
